name: Honeybee
headline: length
subtitle: Worker of the western honey bee, Apis mellifera
description: The western honey bee is a moderately hairy, elongated bee, black to amber brown with a striped abdomen, native to Europe, Asia and the Middle East and now kept around the world. Most bees in a hive are sterile female workers about 10 to 15 mm long. The single queen and the male drones are larger, and a strong colony can hold 50,000 or more workers.

measures.label: Length (honey bees in general)
measures.note: WSU Extension length for honey bees; castes not separated

facts.text: Workers are smaller than drones but have longer wings.
Workers live 2 to 4 weeks in summer, or up to 11 months if they live through the winter.
Colonies can grow to 50,000 or more workers and last through winter on their stored honey.
A worker's sting is barbed and tears away from its body when used.

sources.publisher: Animal Diversity Web, University of Michigan Museum of Zoology

caveats: No USDA page with a worker body length was found; the lengths come from the University of Michigan's Animal Diversity Web and WSU Extension.
A Colorado State University Extension bee-size chart was fetched, but its extracted text does not reliably pair the length ranges with the bee groups, so it is not used.
No source with a worker bee's body mass was fetched.
